text:
mel: Quick FYI I opened a tiny PR to clarify embed+context limits on the catalog for ember-mini-4b. It also fixes a broken perf permalink and swaps an old SDK snippet. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5188 :wave:

anita: Nice. Which broken link was it?

mel: bench CSV for ember-mini-4b had moved after perf job rename. I pointed it at /bench/ember-mini-4b/2026-03-26/ember_mini_throughput.csv and added a footnote with the rig (v100-32gb, seq=512, dyn-batching=on).

cowen: Two tiny asks: 1) split the limits column into "tokens (max_tokens)" and "context (max_sequence)"; 2) swap the old "client.list_models()" SDK example to `catalog.list_variants()` and show limits keys.

anita: Agreed on the split. For the SDK snippet, use this minimal example: ```python
from redwood import CatalogClient
cat = CatalogClient()
for v in cat.list_variants("ember-mini-4b"):
    print(v['name'], v['limits'])
```

mel: Added that snippet. Also added a one-line compatibility note: "Quantized variants may expose lower max_sequence; always read variant limits before pinning."

perf-bot: Artifact check: /bench/ember-mini-4b/2026-03-26/ember_mini_throughput.csv -> OK.

docs-bot: Lint: table cell >120 chars at /catalog/variants.md line 412. Suggest moving rig details to a footnote.

cowen: Move the rig note to a footnote and shorten the inline bench cell to keep table mobile-friendly.

mel: Done  moved rig to footnote and shortened the inline text. Pushed.

anita: One more tiny migration bullet request: include a deterministic diff example (temperature 0.0 + top_k 1) so folks can detect tokenization shifts.

mell: Added shell snippet: `redwood eval --model ember-mini-legacy --model ember-mini-4b --prompt-file smoke.txt --temperature 0.0 --top_k 1 --output diffs.json`.

docs-bot: All checks passed except external links scan shows a 301 for /sdk/cli -> recommend separate PR to update SDK hrefs.

cowen: Fine to follow-up on hrefs. Approving once CI goes green.

mel: Thanks all  merging after CI. Will open follow-up PR for SDK hrefs and a tiny docs CI check that validates benchmark permalinks.
